title: Linkability of Student Identity to Assignment Submission
description: Student's identity (student id) is linked to their assignment submission data (work file, course, timestamp), enabling correlation of multiple submissions to a single student across time and courses.
assumptions: Student ID is included in submission data and is not anonymized.

title: Disclosure of Assignment Data to Unauthorized Parties
description: Assignment data (work file, student id, course, submission timestamp) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network and stored in system without adequate access controls.

title: Usurpation of Student Identity During Login
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate a student during the login process to submit assignments on their behalf.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism may be vulnerable to credential theft or session hijacking.

title: Data Alteration of Assignment Submission
description: Assignment data could be altered during transmission or storage, compromising integrity of submitted work.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network and stored without adequate integrity checks.

title: Unnecessary Personal Data Storage in Assignment Store
description: The Assignment & Grading Service stores student ID, course, and submission time in the Assignment Store. This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal data is transferred to storage. The threat arises if this storage is not strictly necessary for the grading function, or if the data retained exceeds what's needed for legitimate grading purposes.
assumptions: Student ID and course information are personal data; storage duration may exceed necessity
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context about data disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary

title: Linkability of Stored Assignment Data
description: The stored assignment data (student ID, course, submission time) could be linked with other data sources (e.g., student profiles, course rosters, other submissions) to create a comprehensive profile of the student. This linkability threat exists at the storage boundary where data is retained.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that could be linked; student ID is a unique identifier
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on external data sources not modeled in this flow

title: Identifiability of Student from Stored Assignment Data
description: The stored data includes student ID which directly identifies the student. Even with course and submission time, the combination could identify the student in certain contexts, especially if the assignment is unique or course enrollment is limited.
assumptions: Student ID is a direct identifier; course enrollment may be small
uncertainty_note: Identifiability depends on context and whether student ID is anonymized

title: Teacher Identity Usurpation During Login
description: An attacker could impersonate a teacher during the login process, gaining unauthorized access to the Grades Portal Web App and potentially accessing student submission data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanism is not sufficiently secure or teacher credentials are compromised.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable node for identity usurpation threats at ExternalEntity login point.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Submission Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose student submission data to unauthorized parties, either through improper access controls, data leakage, or insecure transmission during the review process.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly enforced or data is transmitted without adequate encryption.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard disclosure threat node for data handling processes.

title: Identifiability of Student Submissions
description: Student submission data processed by the Grades Portal Web App may contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify students, potentially violating their privacy expectations.
assumptions: Student data includes identifiable information and is not adequately anonymized or masked.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data, which fits the submission review scenario.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service writes sensitive student grade data to the database. Without proper access controls, unauthorized actors could read or exfiltrate grade records containing student IDs, grades, and feedback.
assumptions: Database lacks adequate authentication/authorization controls
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard database security practices may not be fully implemented

title: Student and Grader Identification from Grade Records
description: Grade records contain student ID and grader ID, enabling identification of both students and grading personnel. This could lead to privacy violations if accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student and grader identities are directly exposed in the data
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether IDs are anonymized or pseudonymized

title: Grade Record Data Integrity Compromise
description: Grade records could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during storage or retrieval, affecting academic integrity and potentially enabling grade manipulation attacks.
assumptions: No adequate integrity controls or audit logging in place
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard database without integrity constraints

title: Grader Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate a grader to write or modify grade records, potentially submitting fraudulent grades or feedback under another grader's identity.
assumptions: Weak authentication or no grader verification before writing

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation for Student Data
description: Storing student grades with identifying information may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other education privacy regulations if data is not properly protected or if access is not restricted to authorized personnel.
assumptions: Data handling may not meet regulatory requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific regulatory requirements

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades to third parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App may transmit student grades and feedback to unauthorized parties, including system administrators, third-party services, or through insecure data transmission channels.
assumptions: System may have inadequate access controls or data transmission encryption

title: Unauthorized access to student grades by other users
description: Other students, faculty, or unauthorized personnel may access a specific student's grades and feedback without proper authentication or authorization controls.
assumptions: Authentication and authorization mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Data deception through inaccurate grade representation
description: The system may display incorrect, outdated, or manipulated grades and feedback to the student, potentially due to data synchronization issues or intentional tampering.
assumptions: Data integrity controls may be weak or system may have bugs

title: Linkability of student identity to academic records
description: The system may link the student's identity to their grades and feedback in ways that could be exploited for profiling or tracking purposes beyond the intended educational context.
assumptions: System may retain detailed logs or metadata that could be used for re-identification

title: Identifiability of student through grade patterns
description: The combination of grades, feedback, and timing information may uniquely identify the student even if direct identifiers are removed, enabling deanonymization attacks.
assumptions: Grade patterns may be distinctive enough to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured.
assumptions: Network traffic is not encrypted or authentication mechanisms are weak
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats at flow level

title: Linkability of grades to student identity
description: The displayed grades and feedback could be linked to the student's identity, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Student identity is associated with the displayed grades
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a reasonable node for linkability threats at destination

title: Usurpation of student account access
description: If the student's credentials are compromised, an attacker could impersonate the student and access their grades and feedback, potentially misusing the information.
assumptions: Student account credentials are stored or transmitted insecurely
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a reasonable node for usurpation threats at external entity

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) may disclose sensitive grade information to unauthorized parties if authentication/authorization controls are insufficient. Grades are sensitive personal data that could be exposed through vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: The system has vulnerabilities in authentication, authorization, or data transmission that could allow unauthorized access to grade data.

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: An attacker could impersonate a parent and access another parent's child's grades if authentication mechanisms are weak. This would allow unauthorized access to sensitive educational information belonging to other families.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks.

title: Linkability of Parent Identity to Child Grades
description: The system may create linkable records that connect a parent's identity to their child's grades, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across different services. This could violate privacy expectations if the linkage is not necessary for the service.
assumptions: The system stores and processes data in a way that creates identifiable links between parent and child information.

title: Identification of Child Through Parent Request
description: The system identifies the child through the parent's request, potentially exposing the child's identity to the system and potentially to other parties if the child's information is not properly protected or anonymized.
assumptions: The child's identity is transmitted or stored in a way that could be exposed or linked to other data.

title: Linkability of grades data to other child information
description: Parent may link the displayed grades, feedback, and submission history to other information about the child (e.g., from other systems or personal knowledge), creating a comprehensive profile of the child's academic performance and behavior.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources about the child or can infer connections through the grades data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades data
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data logging mechanisms that expose sensitive academic information.
assumptions: System has vulnerabilities or inadequate access controls that could expose data to unauthorized entities.

title: Usurpation of parent identity to access grades
description: An unauthorized third party may usurp the parent's identity to access the child's grades, feedback, and submission history through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised or social engineering attacks are possible.

title: Non-compliance with FERPA and privacy regulations
description: The system may not comply with FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act) or other educational privacy regulations regarding disclosure of student information to parents, potentially exposing the institution to legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: System may not have proper compliance controls or documentation for regulatory requirements.

title: Administrator Account Compromise
description: School Administrator credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized account creation, modification, or disabling of parent-child links
assumptions: Administrator credentials are stored or transmitted insecurely

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: Administrator could access or expose sensitive parent-child relationship data (names, emails, roles) to unauthorized parties
assumptions: Administrator has excessive access privileges or data is logged without proper access controls

title: Action Non-Repudiation Failure
description: Administrator actions (account creation, modification, disabling) could be denied or not properly attributed due to inadequate audit logging
assumptions: Audit logs are incomplete, tamperable, or not properly implemented

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: System may collect more personal data than necessary for account management (e.g., storing full names, emails, relationship details beyond what's needed)
assumptions: Data retention policies are not aligned with minimum necessary principle

title: Identification of Students and Family Members via Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records containing parent-child relationship links to the account directory. This data could be used to identify individual students and their family connections, potentially revealing sensitive personal information about family structures.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiable information about students and their family relationships

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Account Records
description: The grading service writes account records to the account directory. If the data store is not properly secured, sensitive student and family information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through direct access or data exfiltration.
assumptions: The account directory may be accessible to unauthorized entities

title: Tampering with Account Records and Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes account records and parent-child relationship links. Malicious actors could potentially modify these records to alter student identities, family relationships, or grading information, leading to data integrity issues.
assumptions: The write operation is not adequately protected against unauthorized modification

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Record Writes
description: When the grading service writes account records to the directory, there may be insufficient audit logging or cryptographic signing to prevent denial of actions. This could allow the grading service to deny having written certain records.
assumptions: Audit trails or non-repudiation mechanisms may be incomplete

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary.
assumptions: Third-party provider has access to complete personal data including grades and account information

title: Identifiability of Students via Grade Records and Account Directory
description: Grade records and account directory contain personally identifiable information that can directly identify individual students. Transfer to external provider increases identifiability risk.
assumptions: Grade records and account directory contain unique student identifiers

title: Linkability of Personal Data Across Systems
description: Account directory data transferred to cloud provider can be linked with other data sources (e.g., student IDs, names) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.
assumptions: Cloud provider may have access to additional data sources or metadata

title: Data Integrity During Transfer to External Host
description: Nightly backup and replication of sensitive grade and assignment data to external cloud provider creates risk of data tampering or corruption during transmission.
assumptions: Data in transit or at rest on external provider could be modified

title: Unauthorized Use of Disclosed Personal Data by Third Party
description: Cloud hosting provider EE5 may have unauthorized access to or misuse of student grade records, assignments, and account directory information.
assumptions: Third party may not have adequate security controls or privacy policies

title: Regulatory Compliance Risk for Cross-Organizational Data Transfer
description: Transfer of personal data to external cloud provider may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) regarding cross-border or third-party data transfers.
assumptions: Data transfer may not comply with applicable privacy laws

title: Student Identifiability from Grade Records
description: Grade records may contain student identifiers or quasi-identifiers that could allow identification of individual students when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Grade records include student IDs or names, or can be linked to student identities through other means.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grade Records
description: Grade records accessed by the Assignment & Grading Service could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the service or improper access controls.
assumptions: The grading service has access controls that may not be properly enforced, or the data flow could be intercepted.

title: Linkability of Grade Records to Other Data
description: Grade records read by the Assignment & Grading Service could be linked to other student data (e.g., demographic, behavioral) creating a comprehensive profile.
assumptions: The grading service has access to or can correlate with other student data sources.

title: Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The flow of grade records from database to grading service may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding student data handling.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for student grade data, and the current implementation may not meet all requirements.
